subject: science2
loDesc: Classifies kingdom Plantae into Cryptogams (Thallophyta, Bryophyta, Pteridophyta) and Phanerogams (Gymnosperms, Angiosperms - Monocots vs Dicots) based on anatomical characteristics.
hookDemo: Display live specimens of Spirogyra (algae), Moss (Bryophyta), Fern (Pteridophyta), and a flowering plant branch.
hookAsk: Why do mosses and ferns lack true flowers and seeds, and how do they reproduce without seed formation?
streamDo: Observe 5 plant specimens (Spirogyra, Funaria, Nephrolepis, Cycas, Mustard).
streamTask: Classify given plants into Thallophyta, Bryophyta, Pteridophyta, Gymnosperms, or Angiosperms.
mountainTask: Construct a 4-point comparison table contrasting Monocotyledonous and Dicotyledonous plants based on seeds, leaves, roots, and flowers.
skyTask: Differentiate Cryptogams (hidden reproductive organs) from Phanerogams (specialized reproductive tissue and seeds) based on vascular tissue presence.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Assuming Bryophytes (mosses) have true roots, stems, and leaves like terrestrial vascular plants.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Do mosses have vascular tubes (xylem/phloem) to transport water upward?' Introduce rhizoids vs true roots.

crossCurricularLinks: Geography & Agriculture: Crop Botany (Identifying monocot grasses vs dicot legumes in regional farming systems)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Classifies plant kingdom groups based on structural and reproductive features.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Conduct school garden walks to observe leaf venation and root types in monocots and dicots.

subject: science2
fullTitle: Chapter 7: Energy Flow in an Ecosystem
loDesc: Analyzes food chains, food webs, ecological pyramids of energy, and biogeochemical cycles (Carbon, Nitrogen, and Oxygen cycles) in nature.
hookDemo: Display an ecological pyramid diagram showing energy transfer from Producers (10,000 kcal) to Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary Consumers.
hookAsk: Why does energy available decrease at each successive trophic level, preventing food chains from exceeding 4 or 5 steps?
streamDo: Observe grassland food chain components (Grass, Grasshopper, Frog, Snake, Eagle).
streamTask: Identify Producer, Primary Consumer, Secondary Consumer, Tertiary Consumer, and Apex Predator.
mountainTask: Trace the movement of Carbon Dioxide from atmosphere to biotic world via Photosynthesis and back via Respiration and Combustion.
skyTitle: Nitrogen Fixation & Bio-Geo Chemical Cycle Synthesis
skyTask: Explain 4 major processes in the Nitrogen Cycle: Nitrogen Fixation, Ammonification, Nitrification, and Denitrification.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Believing energy cycles continuously through an ecosystem like mineral nutrients do.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Can heat energy lost to the environment by consumers be recycled back to the Sun?' Clarify unidirectional energy flow.

crossCurricularLinks: Environmental Science & Climate: Carbon Footprint (Tracing carbon cycle balance vs fossil fuel combustion emissions)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Understands energy flow across trophic levels and traces biogeochemical cycles.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 10: Use string web models to illustrate food web interconnectedness.

subject: science2
loDesc: Investigates beneficial roles of Lactobacillus, Rhizobium, Azotobacter, and Yeast; examines fungal production of antibiotics (Penicillin) and pathogen diseases.
hookDemo: Add a spoonful of baker's yeast and sugar to warm water in a conical flask, fitting a balloon over the mouth.
hookAsk: Why does the balloon inflate after 20 minutes, and what gas is released during yeast fermentation?
streamDo: Observe micro-organisms: Lactobacillus, Rhizobium, Penicillium, Clostridium, Dengue Virus, Ringworm Fungus.
streamTask: Classify microbes into Beneficial (Industry/Agriculture) vs Pathogenic (Disease-causing) categories.
mountainTask: Explain how Rhizobium bacteria residing in leguminous plant root nodules fix atmospheric nitrogen into nitrates.
skyTask: Explain Alexander Fleming's discovery of Penicillin and discuss why indiscriminate antibiotic overuse causes bacterial resistance.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Taking antibiotics to cure viral infections like the common cold or influenza.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Do antibiotics target bacterial cell walls or viral non-cellular structures?' Stress antibiotic specificity.

crossCurricularLinks: Pharmacology & Public Health: Medical Awareness (Understanding antibiotic stewardship and industrial fermentation processes)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Investigates industrial fermentation, bio-fertilizers, antibiotics, and pathogen mechanisms.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Prepare temporary slides of curd to observe live Lactobacillus rod bacteria under a microscope.

subject: science2
loDesc: Analyzes weather vs climate, meteorology, solid waste management (principles of 7 Rs), and disaster management protocols for first aid.
hookDemo: Display daily weather forecast report charts alongside a climate map of Maharashtra.
hookAsk: What is the key difference between daily fluctuating Weather and long-term regional Climate?
streamDo: Observe waste items: Vegetable peels, Glass bottles, Plastic wrappers, Dry leaves, Used batteries, Electronic circuit boards.
streamTask: Segregate waste into Wet Degradable, Dry Non-degradable, and Hazardous E-waste bins.
mountainTitle: Principles of Solid Waste Management (7 Rs)
mountainTask: Explain 4 key principles from the 7 Rs of waste management: Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, Rethink, Research, Regulation.
skyTask: Outline first-aid emergency procedures for a person suffering from severe bleeding, burns, or sudden fainting (ABC rule).

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Mixing hazardous electronic waste (batteries/circuit boards) in regular wet organic municipal garbage.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'What toxic heavy metals leach into groundwater if batteries break down in soil?' Highlight specialized E-waste handling.

crossCurricularLinks: Civic Administration & Public Safety: Disaster Management (Implementing 7 Rs waste audits and emergency first-aid protocols)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Applies environmental management strategies, waste segregation, and first-aid protocols.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 10: Organize school composting pits for organic wet waste processing.

subject: science2
loDesc: Identifies computer hardware components, software applications, operating systems, uses spread-sheets (Excel) for scientific data processing, and practices cyber safety.
hookDemo: Display a computer motherboard alongside CPU processor, RAM stick, and Hard Disk Drive.
hookAsk: What is the structural difference between primary volatile memory (RAM) and secondary permanent storage (HDD/SSD)?
streamDo: Observe components: Monitor, Windows OS, Keyboard, MS Excel, CPU, Antivirus Software.
streamTask: Classify items into Hardware devices vs Software applications.
mountainTitle: Spreadsheet Formula Application for Science Data
mountainTask: Write down step-by-step MS Excel / Spreadsheet instructions to calculate average marks and plot a bar chart from student test data.
skyTask: Explain cyber threats (Phishing, Malware, Password Theft) and list 4 best practices for safe internet browsing.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Assuming RAM storage capacity determines how many permanent files/photos a computer can store indefinitely.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'What happens to data in RAM when power turns off?' Distinguish volatile workspace memory from persistent storage.

crossCurricularLinks: Computer Applications & Data Science: Spreadsheets (Using Excel charts and statistical formulas for scientific research presentation)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Uses ICT tools for data representation, processing, and understands cyber security practices.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 12: Conduct computer lab sessions on spreadsheet formula creation for scientific charts.

subject: science2
fullTitle: Chapter 15: Life Processes in Living Organisms
loDesc: Explains transportation in plants (xylem and phloem), excretion in plants, human excretory system (nephron structure), and coordination in humans (nervous system and endocrine glands).
hookDemo: Place a celery stalk with leaves in water dyed with red ink for 2 hours, then cut a cross-section.
hookAsk: Why do red streaks appear inside the stalk cross-section, and which vascular tissue transported the colored water?
streamDo: Observe plant transport functions: Water & mineral conduction, Food (sugar) translocation, Unidirectional flow, Bidirectional flow.
streamTask: Classify transport functions into Xylem tissue vs Phloem tissue.
mountainTask: Draw a schematic diagram of a human Nephron and trace the filtration of nitrogenous waste (urea) from blood into urine.
skyTask: Trace the pathway of a Reflex Arc when touching a hot object: Receptor -> Sensory Neuron -> Spinal Cord -> Motor Neuron -> Effector Muscle.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Believing that voluntary brain decisions control rapid emergency reflex actions like pulling a hand away from heat.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Does your hand jump back BEFORE or AFTER you feel pain?' Show that spinal cord reflex arcs bypass brain delay.

crossCurricularLinks: Human Physiology & Health: Neurological Coordination (Mapping sensory-motor nerve pathways and hormonal endocrine feedback)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Explains plant vascular transport, human excretion, and nervous coordination mechanisms.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Use knee-jerk reflex demonstrations to explain involuntary nervous pathways.

subject: science2
loDesc: Understands inheritance of traits, DNA structure (Watson and Crick model), RNA types (mRNA, tRNA, rRNA), chromosomes (karyotype, autosomes, sex chromosomes), and genetic disorders (Down syndrome, Monosomy, Sickle-cell anemia).
hookDemo: Display a 3D double-helix DNA model alongside a human 23-pair chromosome karyotype chart.
hookAsk: Why do children inherit physical traits from both parents while remaining unique individuals?
streamDo: Observe RNA types: messenger RNA (mRNA), transfer RNA (tRNA), ribosomal RNA (rRNA).
streamTask: Match each RNA type with its specific role during cellular protein synthesis.
mountainTask: Construct a Punnett Square for a Monohybrid cross between pure tall (TT) and pure dwarf (tt) pea plants, stating F1 and F2 phenotypic ratios (3:1).
skyTask: Explain the cause of Sickle-cell anemia (hemoglobin gene mutation) and discuss why pre-marital genetic counseling is essential.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Thinking that dominant alleles are always more common or 'stronger' in a population than recessive alleles.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'If a trait is dominant, does it automatically mean 90% of people have it?' Discouple dominance from frequency.

crossCurricularLinks: Genetics & Healthcare: Pre-marital Counseling (Analyzing inheritance probability ratios using Mendelian Punnett squares)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Understands DNA/RNA molecular structure, Mendelian genetics, and chromosomal disorders.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Use Punnett square grid boards for hands-on genetic ratio calculations.

subject: science2
loDesc: Understands plant and animal tissues (simple vs complex), tissue culture techniques, agribusiness applications (sericulture, apiculture, poultry, horticulture), and genetic engineering.
hookDemo: Display sterile test tubes containing plant callus culture growing on nutrient agar jelly.
hookAsk: How can thousands of disease-free plantlets be produced from a tiny tissue explant in a sterile laboratory?
streamDo: Observe tissues: Meristematic, Epithelial, Parenchyma, Xylem, Muscular, Nervous, Connective.
streamTask: Classify tissues into Plant Tissues vs Animal Tissues and state their locations.
mountainTask: List the sequential stages of Tissue Culture: Explant selection, Sterilization, Callus formation, Organogenesis, and Hardening.
skyTask: Analyze economic benefits and modern techniques used in Sericulture (silkworm rearing) or Apiculture (honeybee farming).

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Confusing meristematic dividing tissues with permanent specialized storage tissues in plants.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Which plant tissues actively divide at root tips vs which ones store food?' Distinguish meristem from parenchyma.

crossCurricularLinks: Agronomy & Rural Economy: Agribusiness Scaling (Applying micropropagation and sericulture for high-yield farming)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Understands tissue classification, tissue culture, and modern biotechnology applications in agriculture.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Conduct visits to local tissue culture labs or agricultural research centers.
